Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting;

options noted below:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral or Written Public Comments:

  conference 5 minutes prior. Should any person need assistance with audio, please dial 1-889-
  796-6118. When dialing in, the operator will provide further instructions on how you can make
  public comments via phone.
  ¡ If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception.
  ¡ If you are watching the meeting via Facebook Live or Channel 35 while also accessing the
  phone line, it is requested that you mute the sound of your video as it is offset by 3 seconds from
  the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making public comments on the phone
  line, you will be inaudible due to feedback.

  City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers

the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance

Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in

may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, aid, or service by contacting

Inglewood, California
  July 7, 2020

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  July 7, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:01 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts/Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

  RECOMMENDATION  ADDED  –  RATIFICATION  OF  SBWIB
  APPOINTMENTS. Yvonne Horton, City Clerk, asked the City Council to make a
  motion to include an additional recommendation to Consent Calendar Agenda Item No. 3
  to reflect the adoption of a resolution.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Dotson that the City
  Council does hereby add a recommendation to Agenda Item No. 3 to adopt a resolution.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agenda.
  Dr. Wanda Brown, City Treasurer, spoke concerning the financial report.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Mayor/Successor
  Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated July
  2, 2020, in the amount of $3,123,027.57 are hereby allowed, and check number 674158
  be voided and staff is asked to engage in negotiation with the vendor for a better cost, and
  the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby
  authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  1
 July 7, 2020

 132.6  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims filed pursuant to Government Code Section 913:
  1) Estate of Zavier Portis for negligence on September 8, 2019.
  2) Zedrick Portis for negligence; wrongful death on September 8, 2019.
  3) Kenyetta Taylor-Fields for negligence on September 8, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Franklin that
  the City Council does hereby reject claims listed as A1 through A3. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 101  RESOLUTION NO. 20-89 ADOPTED – RATIFYING APPOINTMENTS TO THE
  SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE INVESTMENT BOARD (SBWIB). Staff report dated
  July 7, 2020, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution ratifying the
  following appointments to the South Bay Workforce Investment Board (SBWIB.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that Resolution
  No. 20-89 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD,  CALIFORNIA,  RATIFYING  VARIOUS
  APPOINTMENTS MADE TO THE SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE
  INVESTMENT BOARD BY MEMBER CITIES

  be adopted to do the following:

  1. On May 22, 2020, the Inglewood Airport Area Chamber of Commerce (IAACC) re-
  nominated Mr. Wayne Spencer, President of Spencer 4 Hire Security, Ms. Maria
  Camacho Director of Government Affairs for the Los Angeles Rams, and Ms. Patricia
  Bennett Owner of P & J’s Unique Bookkeeping & Tax Services, to serve a 4-year term
  of office that commences on July 1, 2020, and will end on June 30, 2024;

  2. On May 4, 2020, the City of Lawndale appointed Mr. Frank Rodriguez, Sales Manager
  for Caliche, Inc. and Casa Bella Properties, to serve a 4-year term of office that
  commences on July 1, 2020, and will end on June 30, 2024;

  3. On April 20, 2020, the Employment Development Department recommended Mr. Ken
  Gomez, Deputy Division Chief for the Los Angeles/Coastal Workforce Services
  Division, to serve a term of office that will end on June 30, 2024;

  4.  On April 20, 2020, the Department of Rehabilitation re-nominated Ms. Susan Senior,
  Regional Director of the Los Angeles South Bay District, to serve a term of office that
  will end on June 30, 2024;

  5.  On March 24, 2020, a replacement nomination letter was sent to the Los Angeles
  County Federation of Labor to consider allowing Ms. Sarah Gonzaga, Mr. Mitch
  Ponce, and Mr. Jeremy Diaz to serve additional 4-year terms of office on the South
  Bay Workforce Investment Board or to nominate other labor representatives to
  represent our multi-city workforce consortium. The letter also requested that the
  Federation of Labor consider allowing Mr. Mike Costigan from the International
  Brotherhood of Electrical Workers to replace Ms. Jane Templin on the SBWIB. An
  objection was not provided by the April 16, 2020 deadline. Ms. Gonzaga, Mr. Ponce,
  Mr. Diaz and Mr. Costigan will be serving a term of office that will end on June 30,
  2024;

  6.  On June 9, 2020, the City of Hawthorne appointed Mr. Marc Weiss, President of
  Commercial Consulting, Inc., to serve an existing term of office ending June 30, 2022;

  2
 July 7, 2020

  7.  On May 14, 2020, California State University, Dominguez Hills nominated Mr. J. Kim
  McNutt, Dean of College of Extended and International Education, to serve on the
  SBWIB under an existing term of office ending June 30, 2022; and

  8.  On June 2, 2020, the City of Redondo Beach appointed Mr. Donald Ford, President of
  Training Education Management LLC, to serve an existing term of office ending June
  30, 2023.

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT APPROVED – COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
  INTERNAL SERVICES DEPATTMENT; PURCHASE ORDER TO LOGANS
  MARKETING COMPANY – APPROVED; THREE-YEAR (3) PURCHASE
  ORDER APPROVED – LOGANS MARKETING COMPANY. Staff report dated
  July 7, 2020, was presented recommending approval of a cooperative agreement to
  purchase Cement.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve a cooperative purchase agreement
  (piggy-back) with the County of Los Angeles Internal Services Department, according to
  Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), Section 2-198.1; 2) Award a blanket purchase order
  to Logans Marketing Company, for the purchase and delivery of cement; and 3) Approve
  a three-year (3) purchase order with Logans Marketing Company for the purchase and
  delivery of cement in the annual amount of $30,000 (total contract amount not to exceed
  $90,000).The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  AGREEMENT  NO.  16-196  APPROVED  –  ENTERPRISE  FLEET
  MANAGEMENT. Staff report dated July 7, 2020, was presented recommending
  approval of Cooperative Agreement No. 16-196 with Enterprise Fleet Management.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 16-196 with Enterprise Fleet
  Management. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  PAYMENT OF INVOICES APPROVED – B&H INGLEWOOD TOW, INC. Staff
  report dated July 7, 2020, was presented recommending approval to pay 206 invoices
  submitted by B & H Inglewood Tow, Inc. (B & H Tow) for services rendered on January
  24, 2012, and from September 22, 2018 through March 31, 2020.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby approve payment of the invoices in the amount of
  $15,512.00. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  AGREEMENT NOT APPROVED – RIDE CO. INC. This item was pulled from the
  Agenda.

 183  FUNDING  ADJUSTMENT  APPROVED  –  THE  INTELLIGENT
  TRANSPORTATION SYSTEMS (ITS) PHASE V. Staff report dated July 7, 2020,
  was presented recommending approval of a funding adjustment for the Intelligent
  Transportation Systems (ITS) Phase V to reflect the required split ratio of 80% funding
  from the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority, and 20% funding
  for the City’s local return.

  3
 July 7, 2020

  It was moved by Council Member Fraklin, and seconded by Council Member Member
  Morales that the City Council does hereby approve a funding adjustment for the
  Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) Phase V. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  PUBLIC  HEARING  SET  –  INGLEWOOD  BASKETBALL  AND
  ENTERTAINMENT CENTER PROJECT. Staff report requesting that a public
  hearing be set to consider the Inglewood Basketball and Entertainment Center Project –
  Certification of the Project Environmental Impact Report No. EA-EIR 2020-045, General
  Plan Amendment No. 2020-003, Specific Plan Amendment No. 2020-001, Zoning Code
  Amendment No. 2020-002, Zone Change No. 2020-001, Ordinance Amending
  Inglewood Municipal Code Chapters 2 (Administration), 3 (Motor Vehicles and Traffic),
  5 (Offenses, Miscellaneous), 10 (Public Works), and 11 (Building Regulations); and
  Sports and Entertainment Complex Design Guidelines and Infrastructure Plan (SEC
  Development Guidelines), and Development Agreement between Murphy’s Bowl LLC
  and the City.

  Mayor Butts ordered the Public Hearing set for July 21, 2020, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

 127  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. Yvonne Horton, City Clerk, commented that the
  nomination period for Council Districts 3 and 4, City Clerk, City Treasurer, School Board
  Trustee Seats 3, 4, and 5 starts on July 13, 2020, and will close on August 7, 2020.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned at the hour of 2:37 p.m.

  Amended this _____ day of __________, 2020

  _________________________
  Yvonne Horton, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
